_comment: Maps SpeciesNet taxonomy strings to display labels. This is config, not code, because the
vocabulary will change as P's tagging habits settle and as the property's species list grows.
taxon_raw is always retained on the detection record, so any mapping decision here is
reversible by re-running the mapping without re-running inference.

_why: SpeciesNet resolves to species level and emits 'mule deer' for O. hemionus. Columbian
black-tailed deer (O. h. columbianus) is a mule deer subspecies and is the ONLY hemionus
subspecies present in CA Zone D-3, so on this property the mapping is unambiguous.
This assumption is property-specific and would be wrong east of the Sierra crest.
Should not occur in D-3 and the USA/CA geofence suppresses it, so a whitetail label here
indicates either a geofence bypass or a genuine oddity. Kept distinct rather than folded
into deer_unspecified so it stays visible.
Genus-level fallback emitted when the classifier cannot separate mule from white-tailed.
Mapped rather than dropped: 'a deer, species uncertain' is useful, a discarded row is not.
The detection where a false negative has real cost. Never filtered by invariant 4.
Property prior (P, 2026-08-16): foxes here are gray fox. Sierra Nevada red fox is an
alpine rarity absent at foothill elevations (95959), so a red-fox species call is a
gray fox misread. taxon_raw retained; reversible by remap if that ever changes.
Property prior (P, 2026-08-16): Sierra foothills, 95959 — the only deer here are
blacktail, so genus/family/order rollups all take the prior. A species-level
odocoileus;virginianus call still maps to whitetail above as an anomaly signal.
SAFETY-RELEVANT. A family-level cat could be a mountain lion, so this must never be
quietly filed as a generic unknown. Listed in review_priority.always_high.
Property prior (P, 2026-08-16): squirrels here are western grays. Family rollup takes
the prior; a species-level otospermophilus;beecheyi call still maps to ground_squirrel
above so a confident ground-squirrel ID stays visible.
Property prior, measured 2026-08-16: all 8 family-level leporid rollups in the first
fully-tagged corpus were human-confirmed jackrabbits, and P's tag vocabulary does not
separate brush rabbit. A species-level sylvilagus;bachmani call still maps to
brush_rabbit above; only the family rollup takes the prior. taxon_raw is retained,
so this is reversible by remap if brush rabbits start appearing.

didelphidae._why: The only didelphid in North America.

cetartiodactyla._why: Order-level fallback; the only wild artiodactyls here are blacktail deer (property prior, 95959).

carnivora._why: Order-level. Could be a lion; treated as high priority.

fallbacks._comment: Applied when no exact match. Order matters; first hit wins.

_comment: Drives ordering in the review queue only. It NEVER filters what is loggable or reachable
(invariant 4). SpeciesNet's calibrated confidence replaces the VLM's self-reported
abstention as the 'surface this for a human' signal.
_always_high_why: unknown_felid and unknown_carnivore are here because a geofence roll-up can turn a
mountain lion into a family- or order-level label. Invariant 4 guarantees such a
detection is still loggable and reachable; putting it at the top of the queue is what
makes it reachable in practice rather than only in principle.
